sections.title: Fraud detection AI: The economics
sections.description: Fraud is one of the largest direct costs in financial services, insurance, and eCommerce. The scale creates compelling AI investment cases.

blocks.heading: Payment fraud
paragraphs: US payment card fraud totals $10B+ annually. For a payment processor handling $100B in annual transaction volume with a 0.10% fraud rate, fraud losses total $100M annually. A fraud detection AI system that reduces fraud rate by 20% saves $20M annually — on a development investment of $80,000–$150,000. Payback: less than 3 days.

blocks.heading: Identity fraud
paragraphs: Account takeover fraud and new account fraud cost US financial institutions $20B+ annually. AI identity fraud detection that analyzes behavioral biometrics, device signals, and application data patterns reduces identity fraud losses by 30–60%.

blocks.heading: Insurance fraud
paragraphs: Insurance fraud costs the US insurance industry $80B annually. Claims fraud detection AI that analyzes claim patterns, medical records, repair estimates, and network relationships reduces insurance fraud losses by 15–40%.

blocks.heading: AML (Anti-Money Laundering)
paragraphs: Banks spend $25B+ annually on AML compliance, including enormous manual investigation cost for transaction monitoring alerts. AI that reduces false positive alert rates by 50–70% saves $5,000–$15,000 per false positive investigation — generating $10M–$100M in annual compliance cost reduction for large financial institutions.

sections.title: Fraud detection technical architecture
sections.description: The technical architecture that enables production fraud detection at scale with sub-50ms latency.

blocks.heading: Real-Time vs. Near-Real-Time vs. Batch
paragraphs: Real-time (< 50ms p99 latency): Required for payment authorization fraud. Requires pre-computed features in Redis, optimized model inference (XGBoost with ONNX export achieves < 5ms inference), horizontal auto-scaling, and circuit breakers.
Near-real-time (< 5 seconds): Account funding transactions, wire transfers, ACH. Allows external data enrichment within the decisioning time window.
Batch (daily or weekly): Insurance claims review, government benefits fraud, AML retrospective analysis. No latency constraint.

blocks.heading: Feature Engineering for Fraud Detection
paragraphs: Payment transaction fraud features: Velocity features (transaction count in 1hr/24hr/7 days), behavioral deviation, network features, device features, time-of-day/day-of-week.
Identity fraud features: Device fingerprint, behavioral biometrics (typing speed, mouse movement), application consistency, network features, velocity.
Insurance fraud features: Claim timing, provider network, claimant history, geographic patterns, treatment patterns.

blocks.heading: Graph Neural Networks for Fraud Ring Detection
paragraphs: Many fraud schemes involve coordinated networks of actors — fraud rings that share devices, IP addresses, bank accounts, addresses, or contact information across multiple fraudulent accounts. Traditional ML models that evaluate each transaction or application in isolation miss the network structure that identifies ring fraud.

Graph neural networks (GNNs) model the relationships between entities — connecting accounts that share devices, transactions that share IP addresses, claims that share providers — and generate embeddings that capture the network context of each entity. Entities embedded close to confirmed fraud in the graph are higher risk even if their individual features appear clean.

ClickMasters builds graph fraud detection using: PyTorch Geometric for GNN development, Neo4j or Amazon Neptune for graph database storage, and streaming graph updates that incorporate new transactions and relationships in near-real-time.

sections.title: Fraud detection compliance requirements
sections.description: Fraud detection AI must satisfy regulatory compliance requirements that vary by industry and fraud type.

blocks.heading: ECOA and Fair Housing Act
paragraphs: Credit-adjacent fraud decisions — loan application fraud screening, account opening fraud screening — are subject to ECOA (Equal Credit Opportunity Act) and Fair Housing Act requirements. Fraud models that reject applications from protected class members at higher rates than non-members create disparate impact liability.

ClickMasters designs credit-adjacent fraud AI with: disparate impact testing across gender, race, and national origin; adverse action reason code design that provides ECOA-compliant explanations; and model audit documentation that satisfies OCC examiner review.

blocks.heading: Bank Secrecy Act and AML Compliance
paragraphs: AML transaction monitoring AI must satisfy Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) requirements: maintaining audit trails of alert generation and disposition, documenting the criteria for SAR (Suspicious Activity Report) filing decisions, and demonstrating that the AI model has been validated for AML effectiveness. OCC model risk management (SR 11-7) requirements apply to AML models at bank holding companies.

ClickMasters builds AML AI with: BSA-compliant audit trail infrastructure, human review workflow for SAR filing decisions (no autonomous SAR filing without human review), and SR 11-7 model documentation for bank AML deployments.

blocks.heading: HIPAA for Healthcare Fraud
paragraphs: Healthcare fraud detection that accesses protected health information (PHI) — patient records, claims data, prescription data — requires HIPAA-compliant infrastructure, BAA execution with covered entities, and minimum necessary PHI access design. ClickMasters builds healthcare fraud AI with HIPAA compliance as standard.

items.answer: ClickMasters designs real-time fraud detection for sub-50ms p99 latency using: pre-computed features in Redis (< 1ms retrieval), XGBoost with ONNX export (< 5ms inference), FastAPI serving with connection pooling, and horizontal auto-scaling. items.question: How do you balance fraud detection accuracy against false positive rates?
items.answer: Precision-recall optimization is calibrated to your specific cost structure: the cost of a missed fraud (false negative) vs. the cost of a declined legitimate transaction (false positive). ClickMasters models the cost-optimal precision/recall operating point from your fraud cost data and calibrates the model threshold to that optimum.

items.question: Can fraud detection AI satisfy OCC SR 11-7 model risk management requirements?
items.answer: Yes. ClickMasters produces SR 11-7 compliant model documentation for fraud AI at bank holding companies: development documentation, validation report, ongoing monitoring plan, and model inventory data elements. This documentation is designed to satisfy OCC examiner review.

items.question: How do you handle graph fraud ring detection?

The GNN generates entity embeddings that capture network context — entities embedded close to confirmed fraud are flagged as higher risk even if their individual features appear clean.
